tracking.known_compatibility_issue: ms-swift 4.4.1 emits several display metrics as strings; SwanLab SDK 0.8.4 rejects those string scalars while numeric training and validation metrics remain available.

conclusion: The eight-GPU ZeRO-3 run completed all 120 training steps, four validations and checkpoint creation. The decreasing validation loss proves that the optimization path worked, but no behavior-quality improvement is claimed because the final Base/Adapter blind-test comparison was not exported before the ephemeral job was cleaned up.
limitations: This is one run and is not a throughput benchmark.
The framework memory metric is a per-rank training metric rather than a sampled whole-card peak.
The adapter checkpoint and prediction files were intentionally stored only in the ephemeral job filesystem and are no longer available.
Validation token accuracy is not a substitute for the fixed 110-example behavior evaluation.
next_validation: Repeat the same fixed-hash run and upload the small comparison metrics before the ephemeral job exits.
Keep Base and Adapter decoding parameters identical and report all six blind-test metrics.
Do not require durable model storage merely to retain the numerical A/B result.
